note: Structured form of docs/5am-run-club-research.md. This is the complete evidence base generated messages are permitted to draw on. Do not add a finding here without a real source.

findings.claim: Sleep/wake regularity, not duration, is the strongest lever. The most-regular sleepers had 20-48% lower all-cause mortality than the least-regular, independent of duration.
findings.source: Windred et al., Sleep, 2024 (UK Biobank, n = 60,977)
findings.implication: Protect the fixed time above all else.

findings.claim: Sleep inertia peaks near the core temperature minimum, which is close to 5AM. Countermeasures with real evidence: bright light immediately, roughly 100mg caffeine, and not snoozing — snoozing re-triggers drift toward deep sleep.
findings.implication: Morning copy should push light and movement, and make snoozing structurally hard.

findings.claim: The cortisol awakening response is a normal 30-75% surge peaking about 30-45 minutes after waking, present in roughly 77% of people.
findings.implication: Reframe grogginess and cold stiffness as expected physiology, not failure.

findings.claim: Morning is not peak performance time — that is late afternoon. Morning wins decisively on adherence instead: the most consistent exercisers train between 4 and 9 AM.
findings.source: Circadian performance rhythms; National Weight Control Registry
findings.implication: Sell consistency and identity. Never promise personal-best pace in the morning.

findings.claim: The 21-day habit rule is a myth. Median time to automaticity is 66 days, range 18-254. Critically, missing one day does not measurably harm habit formation.
findings.implication: The single most important thing the app teaches, because it prevents the what-the-hell effect.

findings.claim: A single lapse can trigger total abandonment of a plan — the what-the-hell effect.
findings.implication: Recovery messaging exists specifically to interrupt this spiral.

findings.claim: Ego depletion, the idea of willpower as a depletable fuel, largely failed to replicate in a 36-lab study (d = 0.06).
findings.implication: Never design around trying harder. Design around friction removal and pre-commitment.

findings.claim: If-then implementation intentions have a real and sizable effect on acting on an intention (d = 0.65).
findings.implication: The night flow forces the user to write a specific if-then plan, not merely read about one.

findings.claim: Identity-based habits reinforce themselves; people infer their own attitudes from their own behaviour, so each action is evidence about who they are.
findings.implication: Frame check-ins as identity evidence, not task completion.

findings.claim: Temporal landmarks such as a new week, a new month, or a birthday reliably boost re-commitment after a lapse.
findings.implication: Use these dates for re-engagement after a miss or a dormant streak.

findings.claim: Effort increases as a reward feels closer.
findings.implication: Progress toward day 66 is a stronger framing than an arbitrary points system.

findings.claim: Injury risk rises when short-term (about 7-day) training load spikes well above the longer-term (about 28-day) average the body has adapted to. The ratio between them is the signal, not either number alone. A commonly cited elevated-risk range starts around 1.5.
findings.source: Gabbett and colleagues, acute:chronic workload ratio literature
findings.implication: Surface the ratio only when it becomes actionable, as advice, never as a gate.

findings.claim: Session-RPE — duration multiplied by a subjective effort rating — is an established load-quantification method used when GPS and heart-rate data are unavailable.
findings.implication: Lets load be tracked with no wearable.
